SFixture: John 6, in the words of the WEB
Pm
V1
TAfter these things, Jesus went away to the other side of the sea of Galilee, which is also called the Sea of Tiberias.
V2
TA great multitude followed him, because they saw his signs which he did on those who were sick.
V3
TJesus went up into the mountain, and he sat there with his disciples.
V4
TNow the Passover, the feast of the Jews, was at hand.
V5
TJesus therefore, lifting up his eyes and seeing that a great multitude was coming to him, said to Philip,
W “Where are we to buy bread, that these may eat?”
V6
THe said this to test him, for he himself knew what he would do.
Pm
V7
TPhilip answered him, “Two hundred denarii worth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one of them may receive a little.”
Pm
V8
TOne of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to him,
V9
T“There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these among so many?”
Pm
V10
TJesus said,
W “Have the people sit down.”
T Now there was much grass in that place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand.
V11
TJesus took the loaves, and having given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to those who were sitting down, likewise also of the fish as much as they desired.
V12
TWhen they were filled, he said to his disciples,
W “Gather up the broken pieces which are left over, that nothing be lost.”
V13
TSo they gathered them up, and filled twelve baskets with broken pieces from the five barley loaves, which were left over by those who had eaten.
V14
TWhen therefore the people saw the sign which Jesus did, they said, “This is truly the prophet who comes into the world.”
V15
TJesus therefore, perceiving that they were about to come and take him by force to make him king, withdrew again to the mountain by himself.
Pm
V16
TWhen evening came, his disciples went down to the sea.
V17
TThey entered into the boat, and were going over the sea to Capernaum. It was now dark, and Jesus had not come to them.
V18
TThe sea was tossed by a great wind blowing.
V19
TWhen therefore they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and drawing near to the boat; and they were afraid.
V20
TBut he said to them,
W “It is I.
W Don’t be afraid.”
V21
TThey were willing therefore to receive him into the boat. Immediately the boat was at the land where they were going.
Pm
V22
TOn the next day, the multitude that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there, except the one in which his disciples had embarked, and that Jesus hadn’t entered with his disciples into the boat, but his disciples had gone away alone.
V23
THowever, boats from Tiberias came near to the place where they ate the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
V24
TWhen the multitude therefore saw that Jesus wasn’t there, nor his disciples, they themselves got into the boats and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.
V25
TWhen they found him on the other side of the sea, they asked him, “Rabbi, when did you come here?”
Pm
V26
TJesus answered them,
W “Most certainly I tell you, you seek me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.
V27
WDon’t work for the food which perishes, but for the food which remains to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give to you. For God the Father has sealed him.”
Pm
V28
TThey said therefore to him, “What must we do, that we may work the works of God?”
Pm
V29
TJesus answered them,
W “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.”
Pm
V30
TThey said therefore to him, “What then do you do for a sign, that we may see and believe you? What work do you do?
V31
TOur fathers ate the manna in the wilderness. As it is written, ‘He gave them bread out of heaven to eat.’”
Pm
V32
TJesus therefore said to them,
W “Most certainly, I tell you, it wasn’t Moses who gave you the bread out of heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread out of heaven.
V33
WFor the bread of God is that which comes down out of heaven and gives life to the world.”
Pm
V34
TThey said therefore to him, “Lord, always give us this bread.”
Pm
V35
TJesus said to them,
W “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
V36
WBut I told you that you have seen me, and yet you don’t believe.
V37
WAll those whom the Father gives me will come to me. He who comes to me I will in no way throw out.
V38
WFor I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me.
V39
WThis is the will of my Father who sent me, that of all he has given to me I should lose nothing, but should raise him up at the last day.
V40
WThis is the will of the one who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.”
Pm
V41
TThe Jews therefore murmured concerning him, because he said,
W “I am the bread which came down out of heaven.”
V42
TThey said, “Isn’t this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then does he say,
W ‘I have come down out of heaven’?”
Pm
V43
TTherefore Jesus answered them,
W “Don’t murmur among yourselves.
V44
WNo one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him; and I will raise him up in the last day.
V45
WIt is written in the prophets, ‘They will all be taught by God.’
W Therefore everyone who hears from the Father and has learned, comes to me.
V46
WNot that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from God. He has seen the Father.
V47
WMost certainly, I tell you, he who believes in me has eternal life.
V48
WI am the bread of life.
V49
WYour fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and they died.
V50
WThis is the bread which comes down out of heaven, that anyone may eat of it and not die.
V51
WI am the living bread which came down out of heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. Yes, the bread which I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.”
Pm
V52
TThe Jews therefore contended with one another, saying, “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?”
Pm
V53
TJesus therefore said to them,
W “Most certainly I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you don’t have life in yourselves.
V54
WHe who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.
V55
WFor my flesh is food indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.
V56
WHe who eats my flesh and drinks my blood lives in me, and I in him.
V57
WAs the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so he who feeds on me will also live because of me.
V58
WThis is the bread which came down out of heaven—not as our fathers ate the manna and died. He who eats this bread will live forever.”
V59
THe said these things in the synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum.
Pm
V60
TTherefore many of his disciples, when they heard this, said, “This is a hard saying! Who can listen to it?”
Pm
V61
TBut Jesus knowing in himself that his disciples murmured at this, said to them,
W “Does this cause you to stumble?
V62
WThen what if you would see the Son of Man ascending to where he was before?
V63
WIt is the spirit who gives life. The flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and are life.
V64
WBut there are some of you who don’t believe.”
T For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who didn’t believe, and who it was who would betray him.
V65
THe said,
W “For this cause I have said to you that no one can come to me, unless it is given to him by my Father.”
Pm
V66
TAt this, many of his disciples went back and walked no more with him.
V67
TJesus said therefore to the twelve,
W “You don’t also want to go away, do you?”
Pm
V68
TSimon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.
V69
TWe have come to believe and know that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
Pm
V70
TJesus answered them,
W “Didn’t I choose you, the twelve, and one of you is a devil?”
V71
TNow he spoke of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, for it was he who would betray him, being one of the twelve.
